report.source_text: An open surgical exploration and washout of the wrist was carried out through a dorsal approach. Three millilitres of purulent and gelatinous tissue was drained from the carpal joint. The intraoperative appearance remained consistent with deep infection, and so infection remained the most likely diagnosis. Tissue samples were obtained for microbiological culture and sensitivities along with concurrent histological and cytological samples, in line with departmental policy.

clinician.final_diagnosis: invasive moderate to focally poorly differentiated basaloid squamous cell carcinoma with focal keratinisation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old male smoker presented with localized left wrist swelling and tenderness after a dog bite, initially treated as infection with raised inflammatory markers and normal wrist X-ray. Symptoms recurred after antibiotics. Eight weeks post-bite MRI showed a 30x21mm inflammatory mass centered on the hamate with extensive marrow abnormality and X-ray showed near complete hamate resorption. Surgical drainage yielded purulent tissue but microbiology cultures were negative. Histopathology confirmed invasive moderate to focally poorly differentiated basaloid squamous cell carcinoma with focal keratinisation, establishing the diagnosis.
